ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Articles L.123-6 and R.123-22-1 of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 and EU AML/CFT obligations. UBO declaration is filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) pursuant to said provisions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry in the country of origin of the corporate shareholder (e.g., ACRA, Companies House)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate resolution authorizing formation of the French SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy or national identity document of each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authority of the beneficiary holder's national state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, legal representative, and ultimate beneficial owner against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List, and the French domestic asset-freezing list (gels d'actifs) under Articles L.561-3 and R.561-2 CMF. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified under the FATF 40 Recommendations and national doctrine, requiring enhanced due diligence with senior management approval before any client relationship or corporate formation is accepted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and Infogreffe RCS database (https://www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin script and be compliant with Article L.123-8 of the French Commercial Code. Non-French words may be allowed if readily expressed in Latin characters, but any prefix, suffix, or expression likely to mislead the public or indicate a national or public function shall be refused. The name must be available in the RCS and must not infringe a registered trademark or create confusion with an existing business name in the same sector.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name by the RCS clerk or the Guichet formalities, the applicant or its attorney may file a written administrative appeal with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the legal grounds for availability and compliance. If the administrative appeal is denied, a formal judicial reassignment may be sought before the Commercial Court held at the registered office location (chambre de la liberté d'établissement), with the assistance of a French Avocat.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for e-commerce and remote activities provided the registered office is domiciled within France and the arrangement complies with Article L.123-11-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. A registered domiciliation company may be used for up to five consecutive years; the address must be a lawful mailing address, capable of receipt of official documents, and must be disclosed to the RCS. For the custom mechanical keyboard keycap sector, a virtual office is acceptable for administrative formalities; however, if physical inventory is retained in France, the business must register a stable French establishment or storage address for customs and tax purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 20% in the first year, rising to 40% if goods are stored or shipped from France, or if the entity registers for VAT and customs operations; unannounced inspections may be conducted by the Direction générale des finances publiques and customs authorities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name search and availability report via Infogreffe
SARL registration filing with the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises and RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of statutory announcement in a French legal journal (JAL)

Apostille and sworn translations of foreign UBO supporter documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent court of the issuing state / French sworn translator

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36; applicable provisions of the French Civil Code and the beneficial-ownership regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) Guichet Unique des Formalités; the local Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés is maintained by the competent commercial court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation (formalité de création) submitted through the Guichet Unique, incorporating the SARL articles of association and registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash capital must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, which issues the deposit certificate. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed and may require an auditor of contributions unless the statutory exemption conditions are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders resolve that the subscribed share capital of the Company is accepted and that each shareholder shall pay the required portion of its cash subscription in accordance with the articles of association. The registered office is established at [full French address]. The shareholders appoint [name] as Gérant for an unlimited term, with authority to represent the Company within the limits of French law and the articles. [Name] is appointed as accounting and administrative officer, subject to the Gérant’s supervision. The Gérant is authorized to complete all bank, registry, tax, beneficial-owner, and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm the SARL structure, business purpose, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités and the competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the proposed company name, corporate purpose, shareholding, management structure, registered office, accounting year, and business activity. Verify that the premises may lawfully be used for plastic injection and storage. Obtain a domiciliation agreement, commercial lease, or proof of ownership. Execute the articles of association in French or with a reliable French translation.
required_dossiers: Registered-office proof dated within the applicable acceptance period
Identity documents of all shareholders and the gérant
Address and civil-status information for the gérant
Corporate documents and powers of attorney for corporate shareholders
Statement of non-conviction and parentage of the gérant
Proposed company name and detailed corporate purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the articles, address evidence, activity description, or identity data and resubmit through the Guichet Unique. Obtain registry clarification where the activity or premises classification is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe and deposit the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, French notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company being formed. Deposit the cash contributions and obtain the capital deposit certificate. Ensure the deposit amount matches the signed subscription schedule and articles. Retain evidence of each shareholder’s contribution and identify any contribution in kind separately.
required_dossiers: Draft or signed articles of association
Bank account-opening forms and source-of-funds evidence where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank compliance queries with ownership, source-of-funds, and business-purpose evidence. Correct discrepancies between the subscription schedule, bank deposit, and articles before requesting the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Culture-approved legal-notice publication service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed incorporation notice to an authorized journal or approved online legal-notice service in the department of the registered office. Verify that the notice states the company name, form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and gérant details. Obtain the publication certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request republication or correction if mandatory information is omitted or inaccurate. Upload the corrected publication certificate to the Guichet Unique if the registry has not finalized the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the company formation and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic company-formation formalité, select SARL, upload the signed articles and supporting documents, identify the commercial activity and premises, and submit the beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the applicable registry and filing charges. Sign electronically using the required authentication method and monitor the filing dashboard.
required_dossiers: Gérant identity document and declaration of non-conviction
Power of attorney, if submitted by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer an INPI or registry request within the specified deadline, replace defective documents, correct activity coding, and resubmit the formalité. An unjustified refusal may be challenged before the competent commercial court under the applicable registry procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate tax and social accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INSEE, Service des Impôts des Entreprises, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET and APE allocation once issued. Confirm VAT, corporate-income-tax, payroll, and employer registrations with the relevant administrations. Convert the provisional bank account into the operating account and maintain statutory accounting records in France.
required_dossiers: Payroll and social-registration records, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the registry, INSEE, tax office, or URSSAF with the Kbis and filing reference to correct missing or inconsistent registrations. Submit amended corporate or tax information where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete industrial-premises, safety, and environmental screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Prefect of the department, Direction régionale de l’environnement, de l’aménagement et du logement (DREAL), municipality, Service départemental d’incendie et de secours (SDIS), and labour authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the plastic-injection installation under the applicable Installations Classées pour la Protection de l’Environnement (ICPE) nomenclature, particularly the plastics-processing provisions. Before operation, determine whether a declaration, registration, authorization, or no ICPE filing applies. Verify planning, fire-safety, worker-safety, noise, waste, wastewater, and storage requirements for the premises.
required_dossiers: Equipment list and rated processing capacity
Waste contracts and safety data sheets
ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization dossier, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DREAL or prefectural requests with revised technical data, capacity calculations, plans, and mitigation measures. Do not commence regulated operation until the applicable ICPE filing, decision, or prescribed waiting period is satisfied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Prefect of the department, supported by the Direction régionale de l’environnement, de l’aménagement et du logement (DREAL), under the ICPE regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE declaration, registration order, or environmental authorization order, if the installation exceeds the applicable nomenclature thresholds; no separate general manufacturing licence is ordinarily required for custom plastic keyboard-keycap production.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, with the competent DREAL and the applicable environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional. The activity is generally subject to an ICPE threshold assessment under the plastics-processing nomenclature. It may require a declaration, registration, or authorization; a full environmental assessment is required only where prescribed by applicable thresholds or screening criteria.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE order, the general requirements for industrial wastewater and emissions, the French order of 2 February 1998 where applicable, local discharge authorization, hazardous-substance controls, VOC and air-emission limits, waste-traceability obligations, and EU waste and chemicals rules. No single universal wastewater or VOC threshold applies independently of the installation classification, process, capacity, and discharge route.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal planning and premises-use confirmation and coordinate fire-prevention requirements with the SDIS. Maintain compliant fire detection, extinguishers, emergency access, evacuation routes, electrical installations, machine guarding, ventilation, chemical storage, and structural floor-load capacity. Complete the employer occupational-risk assessment document, workplace health arrangements, and mandatory inspections. If the premises are open to the public or qualify as an établissement recevant du public, obtain the additional ERP accessibility and fire-safety approvals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; customs and import VAT/cross-border clearance: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal: douane.gouv.fr; centralized company registration via the Guichet Unique administered by INPI and the RCS (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-established SARL: (1) incorporate through the Guichet Unique at INPI; INSEE issues the 9-digit SIREN company number and the SIRET establishment identifier, with registration at the RCS; (2) DGFiP automatically assigns the French VAT identification number using the format FR + 2-digit control key + SIREN; (3) the same VAT number covers all establishment-level VAT filing obligations and must be quoted on invoices, EC Sales Lists and customs declarations; (4) for a non-EU parent/seller without a French permanent establishment, VAT registration is effected with the competent non-resident taxpayer desk (Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères) under Article 283 CGI, normally through an accredited fiscal representative for the standard scheme; alternatively the Non-Union OSS or IOSS schemes may be used for cross-border B2C supplies and low-value consignments; (5) EU-established sellers may elect Union-OSS for distance sales without French domestic registration until the €10,000 pan-EU threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is by default subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (corporate income tax) at the entity level at the standard rate of 25%; French-established profits are taxable in France on a territorial basis, with foreign permanent-establishment profits tax-exempt in France where an applicable tax treaty grants exclusive taxing rights to the foreign State.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (i) pass-through/transparency election under CGI Article 239 bis AA for small 'family-type' SARLs owned by natural persons and meeting the turnover ceiling (€10,000,000) and shareholding conditions, causing the company to be taxed in the hands of the partners; (ii) tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for French groups holding at least 95% of subsidiaries; (iii) VAT fiscal-unity election under Article 256 C III CGI for closely-held French entities; (iv) France applies comprehensive ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules (CGI Articles 208 B, 209-X, 212-1 bis) and offers no domestic 'check-the-box' regime, so entity classification for French tax purposes follows French commercial/Tax Code status and the applicable treaty classification rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR — No general registration threshold for established taxable businesses: any habitual economic activity by a French SARL requires VAT registration from the first taxable transaction (CGI Articles 259 and 283). Small-business relief (franchise en base, CGI Article 293 B and Annex IV) applies to taxable turnover not exceeding €91,900 for supplies of goods and €36,800 for services, but this relief is optional and does not constitute a registration threshold; an exempt business may voluntarily register. For EU-established distance sellers, registration in France becomes mandatory only after the pan-EU intra-Community distance-sales threshold of €10,000 is exceeded (Union-OSS); for non-EU non-established suppliers, mandatory VAT registration from the first supply unless Non-Union OSS is used for B2C e-services or IOSS for imported consignments not exceeding €150.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing for domestic B2B supplies will phase in from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises under the amended reform (Article 85, Loi de Finances 2025); B2C e-reporting obligations follow the same timetable. Acceptable formats: Factur-X (hybrid), UBL and CII; invoices must be transmitted via an accredited PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) API or through the public state portal PPF (Portail Public de Facturation, successor of Chorus Pro). E-invoices must be sent to the PDP/PPF within 2 business days of issuance and B2C transaction data within 10 days of the transaction; no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction control is imposed for the keyboard-keycap manufacturing and e-commerce retail sector, although export/import clearances are processed electronically by DGDDI through the DELTA customs system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate (exonération) applies to supplies of tangible goods physically exported or dispatched outside the EU customs territory (CGI Articles 262-I and 262-ter), provided ownership has transferred to a non-EU buyer and the goods are dispatched/transported out of the EU, with proof of departure generally required within 90 days of the supply; intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers qualify for exemption under Article 262-ter only when the customer's EU VAT number is valid and an EC Sales List (état récapitulatif / DEB) is filed. Services directly connected to exported goods (Article 262-II) are exempt, and B2B services supplied to a customer established in a third country fall outside the French VAT scope under the general place-of-supply rules (Articles 259 and 259-B). Supporting evidence must be retained for six years (LPF Article L102-B). Exporters may claim the resulting input VAT credit through the periodic CA3 VAT return or a refund application (remboursement de crédit de TVA) filed with the competent SIE.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation, ECS) lodged electronically via DELTA and bearing the customs office of exit discharge or digital acceptance reference
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill or Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch of the goods outside the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Justificatif de Rapatriement des Recettes d'Exportation) issued by the credit institution evidencing collection and repatriation of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may retrospectively claw back export VAT exemptions where the documentary evidence is missing, incomplete or inconsistent, generally covering four fiscal years, extended to ten years for concealed or fraudulent activity (LPF Article L169). Penalties under CGI Article 1788-A: 50% of the tax understated for deliberate misconcealment or gross negligence (manquement délibéré) and 80% for fraud (abus de droit or manœuvres frauduleuses), in each case plus late interest of 0.2% per month (intérêt de retard). Independent customs penalties under the French Customs Code apply for false export declarations (fines from €150 to €7,500 per irregularity plus confiscation of goods), and criminal exposure exists for document falsification. Export zero-rating claims are subject to heightened audit scrutiny through cross-referencing of ECS/DELTA customs records, bank remittance data and commercial shipping documents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF, the French central bank), acting with the Direction générale du Trésor of the Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as the banking and payment-institution licensing and AML/CFT supervisory authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. There is no exchange-control licensing, no central-bank permission, no mandatory conversion, and no waiting period for lawful import, export, e-commerce settlement, profit distribution, dividend wire, equity injection, or intercompany loan flows. Administrative requirements are limited to: (i) routing all cross-border payments through an ACPR-licensed bank or payment institution; (ii) providing transaction-level documentation and purpose codes for anti-money-laundering and external-statistics compliance; (iii) reporting cross-border monetary movements above EUR 12,500 to Banque de France where applicable; and (iv) the exceptional foreign-investment notification to the French Treasury under Articles L151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code for non-EU investors acquiring control of a French entity or operating a business branch in sectors of strategic sensitivity. Profit remittance from the French SARL is unrestricted once legally distributable profits exist, the legal reserve obligation of 5% of profits until the reserve equals 10% of share capital is respected, and a shareholder decision is adopted. EU/EEA shareholders receive dividends with no French withholding tax; non-EU shareholders are subject to the domestic 25% withholding rate unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty, and the bank compliance file must evidence the underlying distribution decision and certified accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory-conversion ratio applies to export receipts in France: the mandatory surrender ratio is 0%, and there is no central-bank deadline requiring conversion of USD, GBP, CNY, or other export currencies into EUR. French exporters are free to hold export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts with an ACPR-authorized bank as part of their cash management policy. However, the exporter must ensure that export proceeds are received on or before the contractual due date set out in the commercial invoice, which by French late-payment rules is ordinarily a maximum of 30 days for professional invoices unless the parties agree otherwise; receipts must be traceable to the SARL's actual export transactions and supported by commercial invoices, export customs declarations, bills of lading/airway bills, and bank wire references. Cross-border receipts above the statistical threshold may be included in the obligatory Banque de France external-transaction declaration filed via the credit institution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account ('compte bloqué') for initial paid-in capital, plus Operating Account in EUR and multi-currency foreign-exchange sub-accounts
Operating Corporate Account, Trade-Finance Account, and dedicated inward/outward FX settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank / LCL
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account, documentary credit account, and euro-denominated clearing account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE / Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary settlement rail, Low as a primary treasury architecture. An offshore digital EMI outside the EU/EEA has no standalone passport in France and may not lawfully provide payment services to a French SARL as primary account holder unless the service is provided through an EU-subsidiary or an authorized payment institution operating under the PSD2 passporting framework. French banking monopoly rules under Article L311-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code require all accounts against which cheques or payment orders may be drawn to be held with an authorized credit institution or appropriately licensed payment/electronic-money institution. The SARL should therefore maintain its Tier-1 French bank account as the final settlement point; a non-EU EMI may be used only as a flow aggregator for customer collections, with daily sweeps to the French account and full transaction-level reporting. Any use of an opaque offshore EMI, crypto-based treasury, or shell payment account will create a significant ACPR AML/CFT blocker and may jeopardize the bank relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory mandate that every director must appear physically before a notary or bank branch when the bank deploys an eIDAS-compliant remote identification solution. In practice, Tier-1 French banks almost always require the gérant/manager of a newly formed SARL with non-resident shareholders or beneficial owners to attend one physical KYC interview at the French branch or a certified remote interview with a notary or bank delegate. Directors resident outside France may be represented by a lawfully appointed local manager holding a valid corporate power of attorney, but bank compliance departments will still require comprehensive ultimate beneficial ownership documentation and may request direct communication with the non-resident beneficial owner to verify commercial substance. The senior officers should expect the bank to verify the SARL's registered office, operating business premises, source of funds for the initial capital injection, and the economic rationale for the custom mechanical keyboard keycap manufacturing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident manager or beneficial owner, especially an individual residing outside the EU/EEA, with initial capital injection sourced from a personal, non-business account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passport or national identity documents; recent three-to-six-month personal bank statements evidencing lawful source of funds; tax residence certificate; source-of-wealth statement; business plan for the SARL keycap injection-molding company; supplier purchase orders for PBT resin and double-shot molds; preliminary lease agreement or proof of production facilities; and evidence that the capital injection amount is consistent with the planned cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments routed through or received from low-tax, high-risk, or sanctions-exposed jurisdictions, or through third-party fintech wallets without clear ultimate beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed written supply agreements and purchase orders; pro-forma and final invoices with unique invoice numbers; harmonized-system commodity descriptions for plastic keycaps, tooling, and PBT resin; bills of lading, airway bills, or postal/courier tracking; customs export/import declarations; full transaction mapping from customer order to supplier payment; and corporate documentation of each intermediary, including BO identification where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent or unusually large settlements from payment aggregators such as Shopify Payments or Stripe, which may be perceived as creating an indirect customer relationship that the bank has not directly KYC-screened.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment processor account agreements; merchant identification and verification records; settlement reports showing payout IBAN and frequency; end-user order documentation and invoicing trail; refund and chargeback policy; product website and customer-facing terms; stock keeping unit and pricing evidence for custom mechanical keyboard keycaps; balance-sheet confirmation of revenue recognition; and a clear treasury policy requiring regular sweeps to the French bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-finance red flags such as invoice overvaluation, excessive LC amendments, mismatched goods descriptions, or funding of capital equipment without credible import/export evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturing bill of materials and unit-cost calculations; independent equipment valuations and vendor invoices for injection-molding presses, double-shot tooling, and molds; inspection certificates; shipping insurance; customs valuation declarations; country-of-origin certificates; certificate of analysis for PBT resin; end-customer sales contracts for the novel keycap range; and audited or management-prepared financial statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for the French SARL must be made by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the bank account opened in the SARL's name with an ACPR-licensed French credit institution. The remittance instruction must clearly identify the SARL's full corporate name and legal entity identifier references, and include an ISO 20022 purpose category such as 'EQUI' for equity contribution; if the bank requires a French 'motif de paiement', the code for 'Apport en capital / augmentation de capital' must be used. For capital subscribed before incorporation, the French bank will usually require an 'attestation de blocage' confirming that funds are blocked for the benefit of the company in formation; after registration, the bank will require the manager's resolution approving the capital increase, updated KYC/UBO extracts, and a copy of the statutory deposit certificate. The payment must match the exact amount resolved by the shareholders, name only the actual shareholder as remitter, and carry full source-of-funds evidence. No third-party payment, family-member substitute, or commingled personal-funded transfer should be used. For intercompany loans instead of equity, the payment should be routed with a signed shareholder loan agreement and an intercompany purpose code, with the loan terms clearly documented to satisfy France's thin-capitalization and transfer-pricing rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EUR clearing within the Single Euro Payments Area, the SARL should use SEPA Credit Transfers initiated through EBICS or the bank's corporate e-banking channel, with supporting invoice references and the ISO 20022 purpose category 'TRAD' for trade transactions. For non-EUR disbursements to suppliers outside the EEA, such as USD, GBP, or offshore CNY payments, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 through a Tier-1 correspondent bank, with full beneficiary bank details (SWIFT BIC), invoice number, and commercial contract references. Where documentary credit is required, the French bank may issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700/MT707, with the SARL as applicant and the foreign supplier as beneficiary; the LC must be supported by the export/import contract, pro-forma invoice, transport documents, and certificate of origin. For fast discretionary prepayments to Chinese suppliers, the SARL may use an auditable telegraphic transfer against a supplier invoice and proof of shipment commitment, but should avoid circular or back-to-back payments without underlying goods movement. Shopify Payments and Stripe settlement proceeds should be routed by daily or weekly payout to the French operational account through standard EUR clearing, with all merchant settlement reports retained for the banking compliance file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards under an ISDA Master Agreement or French FBF Master Agreement with an ACPR-regulated financial counterparty, used strictly to hedge commercial EUR/USD and EUR/CNH exposures arising from keycap exports and PBT resin imports.
FX swaps combining a spot transaction with an offsetting forward transaction, permitted for rolling settlement of recurring import and export flows.
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps, permissible when the SARL enters or refinances a foreign-currency shareholder loan or invoice-denominated working-capital facility.
Vanilla European-style currency options, permitted for hedging contingent foreign-currency purchase orders and order-book exposure with bank-qualified counterparties.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or non-deliverable Asian currencies, acceptable only where the underlying currency has local convertibility restrictions, the hedge is clearly documented against real commercial invoices, and the transaction is reported under EMIR and ACPR supervision, without speculative net positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax result declaration (liasse fiscale) — forms 2065-SD and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year accounts: no later than the 3rd working day after 1 May; for off-calendar years: within 3 months of fiscal year-end; electronic filing mandatory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due plus 0.2% monthly late interest; after formal notice, additional 10% penalty; may trigger fiscal tax audit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by shareholders and filing of audited/un-audited financial statements with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Guichet Unique / Infogreffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting to approve annual accounts must occur within 6 months of fiscal year-end; the approved statements must be filed with the RCS within 1 month of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of up to €9,000 for failure to convene the annual shareholders' meeting; administrative fine for non-filing of accounts up to €1,500 (natural person) / €7,500 (legal entity); repeated default can lead to injunction, court-appointed liquidation representative, and removal from RCS (judicial strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner (UBO / bénéficiaires effectifs) declaration update on any shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any direct or indirect beneficial ownership change; no annual re-filing is required if no change occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to €15,000 and/or 6 months imprisonment for directors or representatives; the RCS file is annotated as incomplete and third-party reliance is restricted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business levy (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises — CFE) payment and declaration where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment due 15 December of each taxable year; fractional calls are sent by tax authorities; first-year exemption declaration on form 1447-C-SD must be filed by 31 December of the creation year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% plus 0.2% monthly late interest; failure to declare may result in ex-officio assessment and 10% penalty; prolonged non-payment permits enforced recovery against bank accounts and company assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a French SARL if it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total > €4,000,000, net turnover (excluding VAT) > €8,000,000, average workforce > 50 employees. This company custom-manufactures keyboard caps via PBT injection and typically remains below these thresholds; a voluntary audit remains possible.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général — PCG), including the micro-entity simplified presentation under articles L123-16 to L123-16-2 of the French Commercial Code for small SARL enterprises; IFRS is optional only for consolidated financial statements and not required for this entity structure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French statute imposes no standalone annual UBO resubmission; instead, the SARL must update the beneficial ownership declaration at the RCS within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, new control acquisition, or change in operative control. When annual accounts are filed, the Greffe cross-references corporate data; a change in owners or managers must be disclosed on the annual filing. A director who has actual knowledge of a UBO change and fails to file is liable to criminal penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Securities Movements (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Corporate Officers
Minute Book (registre des délibérations et décisions)
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300–1,200 per year for registered office and legal forwarding services in provincial France; 800–2,000 per year in Paris for a commercial address plus corporate-house handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,500–12,000 for a full statutory audit if thresholds are met; 2,500–6,000 for a voluntary independent financial review of a small manufacturing SARL at average market rates

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% tax rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% for eligible R&D; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs for certain novelty-related expenditure (patenting, design, prototype, etc.).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (statutory no-year-limit); annual offset cap: 50% of taxable profit in excess of EUR 1,000,000 (CGI art. 209).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n°2065-SD (standard liasse fiscale for IS entities) filed through TéléIRIS / impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, the mandatory e-filing deadline is the second business day following 1 May (e.g., 3 May 2025).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: C011 / Box 'Société déclarante' (SIRET, APE, legal form)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the SARL, its business registration number, French APE code, and tax identification details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert only the French SIRET and APE code 3240Z or equivalent; non-resident directors must be disclosed with their residence tax ID and treaty country details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports tangible and intangible assets, inventories of raw PBT caps and finished keycaps, receivables and liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All assets and liabilities of the French trade must be booked in the SARL; foreign parent loans must be evidenced with interest at arm's length and disclosed in the credit-related notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Captures e-commerce sales (Shopify) and payment-facilitator gross settlements, procurement costs, salaries, marketing, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue revenue on a delivered-caps basis; payments routed through Stripe/Shopify must be reconciled to the underlying customer invoices with no omission of foreign e-commerce turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shows the cost basis and depreciation of injection moulds, tooling, and quality-control equipment; includes capitalised software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Independent expert valuations are recommended for inbound intra-group mould transfers; avoid using undervalued transferred assets to inflate future deductible depreciation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065 / Box 'Résultat fiscal et calcul de l'IS'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Completes the taxable profit, applies carryforward losses, credits, and reduced rate to determine final corporate income tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not take manufacturing profit offshore; the French SARL should preserve its taxable absorption of any extra-statutory losses before dividend distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers progressive surcharges: 10% (unfiled before demand), 20% (filed within 30 days of a formal notice), 40% (filed after 30 days), or 80% (repeated default), plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (CGI arts. 1728, 1731).
